summary: Atlan is an interactive 3D globe built with CesiumJS that maps Earth, Moon, and Mars sites to show why terrestrial locations serve as analogs for lunar and Martian exploration. It visualizes analog sites across three bodies — spanning India, the USA, and locations worldwide on Earth, along with key targets on the Moon and Mars. Each site is tagged with geology, NASA POWER climate data, and twin-site links explaining why a desert in Rajasthan mirrors a Martian plain or a lava tube in Karnataka resembles a lunar cave. Users can switch between Earth, Moon, and Mars globes with real NASA imagery (LRO WAC, Viking, THEMIS, CTX), toggle 2D/3D views, browse overlay layers like temperature and vegetation, and compare sites side-by-side at true scale. Shastra, a built-in AI assistant, answers questions about any site or region. The comparison system rates each Earth site against its Moon/Mars twin across eight dimensions — terrain, geology, thermal, water, atmosphere, biology, subsurface, and operations — making it clear where the analogy holds and where it breaks down.
details:
Atlan is a 3D interactive globe that lets you explore Earth, Moon, and Mars side by side. It shows locations on Earth that closely resemble places on the Moon and Mars, helping scientists and space agencies understand where to test equipment, train astronauts, and study geology before actual missions.

What it does:

The app displays analog sites across all three bodies. Each Earth site is linked to a twin on the Moon or Mars with an explanation of why they match. For example, the Lonar Crater in India is linked to lunar impact craters because both share similar basaltic rock and impact structures. Users can click on any site to see its geology, climate data, elevation, and a detailed comparison with its twin.

How it works:

The globe is built using CesiumJS with real NASA imagery. Moon tiles come from NASA LRO and JAXA Kaguya. Mars tiles come from NASA Viking, THEMIS, and MRO CTX missions. Earth climate data is pulled from the NASA POWER API covering temperature, precipitation, pressure, solar radiation, and more. The side by side comparison reprojects satellite imagery from both bodies into the same scale so you can visually compare terrain features at their true size.

How we compare sites:

Each Earth site is rated against its Moon or Mars twin across eight dimensions: terrain, geology, thermal environment, water activity, atmosphere, biology, subsurface structure, and operational suitability. These scores are based on published research and NASA mission data. The app also shows where the analogy breaks down, because no place on Earth perfectly replicates another world.

Tools used:

React, TypeScript, Vite, CesiumJS, NASA Trek tile servers, NASA GIBS overlays, NASA POWER API, and Cesium Ion for optional 3D terrain. Shastra, a built in AI assistant, answers questions about any site or region on the map.

Why it matters:

Space agencies spend significant resources choosing where to simulate extraterrestrial conditions on Earth. Atlan puts all that information in one place with real data, real imagery, and an honest breakdown of what matches and what does not. It is designed to be a practical tool for mission planners, researchers, and students exploring planetary science.
